Industrial AI
AI in Oil and Gas: Real Use Cases, Data Sources, Challenges and a Downtime ROI Calculator

Oil and gas companies now run machine learning on the same sensor data your transmitters send to SCADA every second. Here you will see where it pays off, which companies report real results, and how to plan a small pilot that survives.

Predictive Maintenance Seismic & Drilling Leak & Methane Detection Pilot Plan ROI Calculator

AI in oil and gas has moved from slide decks to control rooms, with operators reporting large measured savings. Learn the use cases, data, risks and how to estimate pilot payback.

Hello everyone, today we are going to learn ai in oil and gas, the real use cases, the data it needs, the challenges and how to calculate the return on a pilot.

What Is AI in the Oil and Gas Industry?

AI in oil and gas means using machine learning, computer vision and language models on field data to predict equipment failures, interpret seismic data, optimise drilling and production and detect leaks or emissions. It does not replace the DCS, SCADA or safety system, it reads their data and gives earlier warnings.

Quick Answer
  • Most value today comes from predictive maintenance of pumps, compressors and valves
  • Shell, Equinor and ADNOC publicly report large scale programmes with measured value
  • The raw material is historian and SCADA data from ordinary field instruments
  • Data quality, OT security and explainability decide whether a model is trusted
  • Start with one asset class, one clear failure mode and a cost based business case

New to the basics? Read artificial intelligence and machine learning and how AI connects to PLC, SCADA and DCS first.

AI in Oil and Gas Use Cases With Real Company Examples

The table maps each use case to its data and a company with published results, each from a named public source.

Use caseMain data usedPublished example
Predictive maintenanceVibration, temperature, pressure, flow from the historianShell with C3 AI, over 10,000 assets (JPT)
Seismic interpretation3D seismic volumes, well logsEquinor, about 10 times faster interpretation (JPT)
Drilling optimisationDrilling plans, geology, past drilling time and costAramco Metabrain, ONGC deepwater wells
Production optimisationWell and facility sensor data in a command centreADNOC Panorama and AIQ tools (World Oil)
Pipeline leak detectionPressure and volume data from CPM and SCADAPHMSA funded PRCI study by Southwest Research Institute
Emissions and flare monitoringMethane sensors, drones, satellitesTotalEnergies MethaneLive, ADNOC Emission X
Computer vision for safetyCCTV video streamsADNOC SMARTi hazard detection
Generative AI for documentsReports, procedures, drawingsTotalEnergies lab with Mistral AI, Aramco Metabrain

Predictive Maintenance for Compressors and Pumps

Most operators start with rotating equipment, because a tripped compressor stops production. According to the Journal of Petroleum Technology, Shell scaled its C3 AI programme to more than 10,000 pieces of equipment, including control valves, pumps and compressors, using more than 3 million sensors and nearly 11,000 machine learning models.

The same JPT report says the system makes more than 15 million predictions per day and processes about 20 billion rows of data every week. The idea is simple: learn the normal pattern of each machine and flag drift long before a vibration alarm or trip would occur.

10,000+Shell assets under AI monitoring
15 millionShell predictions per day
700+Equinor rotating machines monitored
$120 millionEquinor maintenance savings since 2020

Equinor reports a similar story, with more than 700 rotating machines and about 24,000 sensors monitored, and estimated predictive maintenance savings of $120 million since 2020, according to JPT. For the theory behind these models, see this guide on machine learning for predictive maintenance and compare it with classic predictive and preventive maintenance.

Do You Know?

Equinor notes that predictive maintenance also cuts emissions, because fewer sudden shutdowns means less emergency flaring and lower CO2 release.

Seismic Interpretation and Drilling Optimization

Seismic interpretation is a pattern recognition problem, which suits deep learning well. Equinor says AI now analyses seismic data about 10 times faster, and in 2025 it interpreted data covering 2 million square kilometres of the Norwegian continental shelf, as reported by JPT.

Offshore Technology reports that Aramco built Metabrain, a generative model with 250 billion parameters trained on seven trillion data points. Aramco says it uses drilling plans, geology and past drilling cost to recommend well options.

Quick Tip

An AI drilling advisor is only as good as the depth, weight on bit and torque data behind it, so check sensor calibration and time stamps before blaming the model.

Production Optimization and Pipeline Leak Detection

World Oil reports that ADNOC generated $500 million in value in 2023 from more than 30 AI tools, run from centres such as its Panorama Digital Command Center. Its CPAD tool monitors critical equipment remotely, and Robowell remotely operates upstream equipment such as flow valves.

Pipeline leak detection is a harder test. A PHMSA research project carried out by Southwest Research Institute for PRCI cites a study in which computational pipeline monitoring found only 20 % of hazardous liquid leaks and SCADA found 28 % between 2010 and 2012.

The project used machine learning to help CPM software find smaller leaks, though PHMSA notes its dataset was small. Pressure transients such as negative pressure waves remain a key input.

Emissions, Flare Monitoring and Computer Vision for Safety

Oil Review Middle East reports that TotalEnergies launched MethaneLive, a methane monitoring centre, in early 2026, and it has detected 35 fugitive methane leaks that were then fixed. It installed 13,000 upstream sensors in 2025.

ADNOC's Emission X, built by its joint venture AIQ, predicts emission sources up to five years ahead, according to World Oil. These tools sit on top of measurement systems such as a continuous emissions monitoring system, not in place of them.

The US Department of Energy notes a New Mexico study where fewer than 4 % of sources may cause half of observed leaks. For safety, World Oil says ADNOC uses SMARTi, a computer vision system that detects hazards, much like the AI PPE detection used in plants.

Generative AI in Oil and Gas

Generative AI is mainly used to search procedures, summarise reports and draft work instructions. Oil Review Middle East says TotalEnergies set up a joint lab with Mistral AI that starts with refinery performance analysis and then moves to exploration and production documents.

JPT notes that Equinor staff use copilots, chatbots and agentic AI, while its core operational analytics still rely mainly on traditional machine learning. To understand why language models can sound right but be wrong, read how large language models work and this overview of generative AI in industrial automation.

Advertisement
Do You Know?

Equinor has identified more than 100 new AI use cases, according to JPT.

Machine Learning in Oil and Gas: Where the Data Comes From

Almost every model starts with field instrument data that flows through SCADA into a process historian. How it links to the business network, see SCADA historian integration, decides how easily data scientists can reach it.

Field instrumentsPressure, flow, level, temperature, vibration and gas detectors produce the raw signals
PLC, RTU and SCADASignals are scanned, alarmed and sent to the control room
HistorianTime series data is stored with tags, units and quality flags
Data platformData is copied through a DMZ to a cloud or on site analytics server
ModelMachine learning scores each asset or well and raises a prediction
Operator actionEngineers review the alert and plan maintenance or adjust set points

Challenges: Data Quality, OT Security and Explainability

The biggest blocker for ai in oil and gas projects is data quality: frozen transmitters, wrong units, missing time stamps and maintenance work orders that never record the real failure cause. An anomaly detection model trained on bad data simply learns to accept bad data.

OT security is the second issue, because analytics needs data to leave the control network without opening a path back in. Follow the Purdue model with proper OT network segmentation, and run through the SCADA security checklist before any cloud connection.

Explainability is the third, since a shift engineer will not stop a compressor because a black box says so. Models that show which tags drove the alert get adopted, and AI root cause analysis tools help here.

Myth: AI will replace the control system and operators
Fact: The examples here all advise people or work beside the DCS, and the safety system stays independent
Myth: A pilot that works on one pump will scale automatically
Fact: Shell needed nearly 11,000 models for its fleet, so scaling is a project of its own
Myth: Generative AI is the main source of value today
Fact: JPT reports Equinor core analytics still rely mainly on traditional machine learning
Benefits
  • Earlier warning of equipment failure
  • Fewer unplanned shutdowns and less flaring
  • Faster seismic and well planning work
  • Uses existing sensor data
Limitations
  • Needs clean, well tagged historian data
  • Adds cyber risk if networks are not segmented
  • Black box alerts may be ignored
  • Models drift when operating conditions change
  • Scaling takes time

India Context: ONGC and AI Led Drilling

In India, The Core reported in January 2026 that ONGC is using AI driven analysis for well planning and advanced seismic interpretation to improve its odds in deepwater and ultra deepwater exploration. Chairman Arun Kumar Singh said ONGC has drilled about 60 such wells, with success rates below its target.

The report says ultra deepwater wells can cost nearly 20 times more than conventional offshore wells, so better well placement pays. ONGC aims to save 5,000 to 10,000 crore rupees a year through efficiency and digital integration.

How to Run an AI Pilot in an Oil and Gas Plant

1
Pick one asset class
Choose gas compressors or export pumps with a clear, costly failure mode
2
Check the data
Confirm two years of clean historian data and real failure records
3
Agree the business case
Value one hour of downtime with operations and finance first
4
Secure the data path
Move data one way through a DMZ
5
Build and back test
Train the model and test it on past failures it has not seen
6
Run in advisory mode
Send alerts to engineers for three to six months and log every hit and false alarm
7
Decide and scale
Compare results with the business case, then extend to similar assets

A good pilot also tracks remaining useful life for the chosen machines, so planners know how much time they have. Keep the safety layer, such as a HIPPS system, completely outside the AI scope.

Quick Tip

Count false alarms as carefully as hits, because operators stop trusting a system after a few wrong alerts.

Downtime Cost Avoided ROI Calculator

Use this calculator to estimate the payback of a predictive maintenance pilot from the downtime it avoids. Enter values in lakh rupees, and treat the result as a first estimate for a business case, not a guarantee.

AI Pilot ROI From Downtime Avoided
Result
Saving 240 lakh, net benefit 180 lakh, ROI 300 %, payback 3 months
Solved example with the default values
Saving = 48 h × 5 lakh = 240 lakh
Net benefit = 240 minus 60 = 180 lakh
ROI = 180 ÷ 60 × 100 = 300 %
Payback = 60 ÷ (240 ÷ 12) = 3 months

In this example, avoiding 48 hours of compressor downtime a year at 5 lakh rupees per hour pays back an annual AI cost of 60 lakh in about 3 months. You can cross check the result with a general payback period calculator and then add maintenance and flaring savings separately.

Field Tips: Why AI Pilots Fail

SymptomLikely causeField fix
Too many false alarmsModel trained on start up and shutdown periodsFilter out non running states before training
Model missed a real failureFailure mode not present in training dataAdd physics rules or anomaly detection for rare events
Predictions flat or stuckFrozen transmitter or historian compressionCheck instrument health and compression settings
Alerts ignored by shift teamNo explanation or no ownerShow the top contributing tags and assign a named owner
Good pilot, poor scale upEach asset tuned by handStandardise tags and templates

AI in Oil and Gas FAQ

How is AI used in the oil and gas industry?

It is used for predictive maintenance, seismic interpretation, drilling and production optimisation, leak detection and emissions monitoring. Computer vision checks safety on site, and generative tools search and summarise technical documents.

Most value today comes from predictive maintenance of pumps, compressors and valves. Shell, Equinor and ADNOC have all published results from large programmes running on ordinary historian data.

What is predictive maintenance in oil and gas?

Predictive maintenance uses sensor data such as vibration, temperature and pressure to forecast when a machine will fail. Maintenance is then planned just before the failure instead of on a fixed calendar.

Machine learning models learn the normal pattern of each pump or compressor and flag early drift. Equinor estimates savings of $120 million from this approach since 2020, according to the Journal of Petroleum Technology.

How does AI help in drilling?

AI studies past drilling time, cost and geology to suggest better well locations and drilling plans. It can also warn the drilling crew early about problems such as stuck pipe or poor hole cleaning.

Aramco says its Metabrain model recommends well options from drilling plans and geological data. In India, ONGC is applying AI driven well planning and seismic work to its deepwater exploration programme.

Which oil companies use AI?

Shell, Equinor, ADNOC, TotalEnergies, Aramco and ONGC have all described AI programmes in public sources. Their examples range from equipment monitoring to seismic work and methane detection.

ADNOC reported $500 million in value from AI in 2023, according to World Oil. Equinor reported about $130 million in value and savings in 2025, according to the Journal of Petroleum Technology.

What are the challenges of AI in oil and gas?

The main challenges of ai in oil and gas are poor data quality, OT cyber security and models that operators cannot understand. Frozen transmitters, wrong units and weak failure records ruin training data quickly.

Linking analytics to control networks also adds cyber risk unless the network is properly segmented. Models need clear explanations and named owners, or alerts will simply be ignored by busy shift teams.

What We Learn Today

  • AI in oil and gas delivers most value today through predictive maintenance of pumps, compressors and valves, with Shell and Equinor reporting large measured results.
  • Every model depends on clean historian and SCADA data from healthy field instruments, so instrument engineers play a central role in any successful project.
  • A good pilot starts with one asset class, a costed failure mode, a secure data path and an honest count of false alarms before scaling.
